<fragment>
The best-selling band in history, the Beatles have sold more than 600 million units as of 2012[update].[447][nb 11] From 1991 to 2009 the Beatles sold 57 million albums in United States, according to Nielsen Soundscan.[449] They have had more number-one albums on the UK charts, fifteen,[450] and sold more singles in the UK, 21.9 million, than any other act.[451] In 2004, *Rolling Stone* ranked the Beatles as the most significant and influential rock music artists of the last 50 years.[452] They ranked number one on *Billboard* magazine's list of the all-time most successful Hot 100 artists, released in 2008 to celebrate the US singles chart's 50th anniversary.[453] As of 2017[update], they hold the record for most number-one hits on the *Billboard* Hot 100, with twenty.[454] The Recording Industry Association of America certifies that the Beatles have sold 183 million units in the US, 
</fragment>
<fragment>

The Beatles are the best-selling music act of all time, with estimated sales of 600 million units worldwide.[4][5] They are the most successful act in the history of the US *Billboard* charts,[6] holding the record for most number-one albums on the UK Albums Chart (15), most number-one hits on the US *Billboard* Hot 100 chart (20), and most singles sold in the UK (21.9 million). The band received many accolades, including seven Grammy Awards, four Brit Awards, an Academy Award (for Best Original Song Score for the 1970 documentary film *Let It Be*), and fifteen Ivor Novello Awards. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1988, and each principal member was individually inducted between 1994 and 2015. In 2004 and 2011, the group topped *Rolling Stone*'s lists of the greatest artists in history. *Time* magazine named them among the 20th century's 100 most important people.

The Rolling Stones have sold over 240 million albums worldwide.[434] In 2010, *Rolling Stone* ranked them as fourth on their list of the Greatest Artists of All Time;[435] three years later, *Rolling Stone* declared them the "most definitional band that rock & roll has produced".[422] *The Telegraph* has called Mick Jagger "the Rolling Stone who changed music".[420] The band has been the subject of numerous documentaries and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame by Pete Townshend in 1989.[436][437] The Rolling Stones have inspired and mentored new generations of musical artists both as a band[438][439] and individually.[440][441] They are also credited with changing the "whole business model of popular music".[420] The only artists to top the UK Album Charts in six different decades, they are tied with Elvis Presley and Robbie Williams for the second most number 1 albums on the Official UK Chart, surpassed only by the Beatles.[372]
